newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman CEO mulling Wascana bid.
newsitem.headline: Talisman CEO mulling Wascana bid.

text.p: Talisman Energy Inc was reviewing its options after Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd's announcement today of a rival bid for Wascana Energy Inc, Talisman Chief Executive Jim Buckee said on Tuesday.
But Buckee repeated that his firm would improve its C$1.7 billion cash and stock offer if it could be sure of the extra value.
"We think that it's not a level playing field -- they're not allowing us to see any data," Buckee said in a phone interview.
"We've signalled that we'd move if we saw value. For the moment (we're) just thinking what to do."

Buckee said he was critical of the new deal because of earlier contentions from Wascana executives that Talisman's cash and stock offer meant the target's shareholders would receive less economic reward than they would contribute.
"They said it was unfair because the Wascana shareholders were not entitled to participate in the upside in pro rata fashion," he said.
"In this particular case, Wascana's (holders) have zero chance of continuing in the upside."
CanOxy, in a deal that had the blessing of Wascana's board, said on Tuesday it would offer C$20.50 per share in cash for the Regina-based producer.
Buckee called into question the potential tax hit on Wascana investors who tender to CanOxy's offer.

"Seeing how Wascana's shares had wallowed in the C$12 range for a year and a half, there will be a lot of people with a tax base at about C$12.50. If now they're forced to accept cash, they've got tax leakage of up to C$3," he said.
"When the tax is taken into account, it's not clear that this is a better offer."
Buckee said he did not know whether Wascana would grant his firm access to its data room now that there was a rival offer on the table.
